page_title: mirroir-mcp: real iPhone automation for AI agents over MCP

sources.entry: mirroir-mcp - Open-source MCP server and CLI that lets AI agents see, tap, swipe and type on a real iPhone through iPhone Mirroring, without Developer Mode or Xcode. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jfarcand/mirroir-mcp) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: mirroir-mcp
summary.one_liner: Open-source MCP server and CLI that lets AI agents see and control a real, stock iPhone through iPhone Mirroring, with no Developer Mode, Xcode or WebDriverAgent.
use_cases: Let an AI agent operate apps on a real iPhone via natural-language prompts
Create or edit calendar events and send messages through an agent
Run repeatable UI regression tests on a stock iPhone in CI
Explore an iOS app and generate reusable SKILL.md workflows
Run combined web and iPhone test scenarios from one YAML file
Convert existing Maestro flows to run on a physical iPhone
summary.what_it_does: The tool exposes 39 MCP tools that let an AI agent observe the iPhone screen (screenshots, OCR-based describe_screen with tap coordinates) and act on it (tap, swipe, type_text, press_key, launch_app, and more) through macOS iPhone Mirroring. An agent can explore an app breadth-first and generate SKILL.md bundles, then save compiled coordinates so the flow replays from the CLI without an LLM. The companion mirroir-run tool validates and runs YAML scenarios across iPhone, Playwright-driven web pages, HTTP and processes, and reports a distinct DRIFT verdict (exit 65) when output moves past its baseline. Permissions are fail-closed: without a config file only read-only tools are exposed, and blockedApps can exclude apps such as Wallet or Banking.
notable: Works on a stock iPhone via iPhone Mirroring: no Developer Mode, signing, Xcode or on-device agent
Replay recorded skills without an LLM, with a DRIFT verdict for output changes
mirroir-run runs one scenario across iPhone, Playwright web pages, HTTP and processes, and runs web/process/HTTP steps on Linux CI
caveats: Requires iPhone Mirroring on macOS; no Android or iOS Simulator support
macOS target support is experimental and needs the MCP client and target window in the same Space
Multi-touch and twin-stick style games are out of reach because iPhone Mirroring exposes a single pointer
